title: fig-mnist-roofline: the running network on two rooflines
caption: Attainable FP32 rate vs arithmetic intensity for a desktop CPU and a data-center accelerator, with the running network marked at batch 1 (~0.5 FLOP/byte) and batch 32 (~12). Both points sit left of both ridge points (~20), the cleanest statement that this workload is bandwidth-bound and batching climbs the slope.

title: The two coupled passes
caption: Forward pass recording activations, backward pass consuming them in reverse; the turnaround is where saved-activation memory peaks. Our four-states.svg prices the same picture per term.

title: The composite USPS inference pipeline
caption: The book's six-stage composite shared by ZIP-code research and check readers: acquisition, preprocessing, neural scoring, thresholding, decision, review. Our reject-gate.svg abstracts the same shape around the threshold.

title: Handwritten address variability
caption: Real envelope city names and ZIP codes from the USPS database: cursive slant, uneven stroke width, broken loops, textured backgrounds. The variability preprocessing had to absorb before any network saw a digit.

title: Matmul share of the forward pass
caption: The book's margin figure on matrix multiplication's dominance: bias, activation, and softmax terms contribute a negligible fraction next to the matmul rows, which is why 'count the matmuls' is the whole cost model.

title: Training vs inference memory budget table
caption: The per-term byte table behind the ~3x ratio at batch 32: persistent parameters vs gradients, optimizer state, and saved activations. Worth auditing line by line against the four-state equation.

title: Early ZIP-code recognition results
caption: The 1989 measured point: 1% classification error on accepted digits after rejecting 12.1%, and the throughput drop from >30 to 10-12 classifications/s once acquisition is included. One point on the risk-coverage curve.
